To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated a new concept of electrolyte-gated ion-selective sensors based on carbon nanotube networks, which can be used to selectively measure the concentration of primary ions in the micrometer concentration range in the presence of highly concentrated background ions.
we demonstrate the selective detection of primary ions in a highly concentrated background electrolyte by electrolyte-gated field-effect transistors based on carbon nanotube networks.

we demonstrate a flexible electrolyte-gated ion-selective sensor based on a carbon nanotube field-effect transistor, which is selective for K+ and Ca++ ions, with a detection limit of 10-6 M and 10-5 M for K+ and 10-6M and 10-4 M for Ca2+, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials, methods, and technologies for the fabrication of novel electronic components and devices.
the development of novel flexible, low-cost, portable and multiplexed sensors for the detection of primary ions in complex media, such as biological samples or environmental solutions.
the development of new materials for biosensors and the investigation of their properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is a promising route towards the realization of flexible, low-cost, portable and multipurposed biosensors.
the work presented in this thesis is a significant contribution to the field of carbon nanotube-based biosensing.
this paper demonstrates the use of carbon nanotubes for the fabrication of flexible, portable and selective sensors for primary ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the ion-selective properties of electrolyte-gated field-effect transistors with carbon nanotube networks as the semiconductors.

we have demonstrated the ion-selective sensing of two prominent second messeners, K+ and Ca+2, by electrolyte-gated field effect transistors (EG-FET) based on carbon nanotubes (CNT) on flexible substrates.
we have developed an electrolyte-gate field-effect transistor based on a flexible substrate and carbon nanotubes as the semiconductors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of electrolyte-gated field-effect devices based on carbon nanotube networks can be successfully exploited for the development of flexible ion-sensitive sensors.
carbon nanotube-based sensors can be used to selectively detect ions in a complex background of interfering ions and can be integrated into flexible devices.
the electrolyte-gated ion-selective sensors are highly promising for the development of flexible biosensing devices for the detection of a wide variety of ions in physiological solutions.
